land.text: the Safavid realm held by Nader as regent since 1732: Iran, Herat and the Caucasus reconquered 1730-1735

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps a tiny Safavid shape (298 km2) to 1737 and draws the real realm as 'Afsharid Iran' from 1734.

land.text: Mashhad and Khorasan, taken by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1796
Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar (1747) and Herat (1750)

successors.note: Land passed in 1747-1750, long before the end; the Afsharid page names the Durrani Empire among the successors.

rulers.name: Nader Shah
rulers.note: Assassinated at Quchan on 20 June 1747 (Nader Shah page); regent for Abbas III from 1732.

rulers.name: Ebrahim Afshar
rulers.note: Set himself up as a rival to Adel Shah.

rulers.name: Shahrokh Shah
rulers.note: Proclaimed at Mashhad on 1 October 1748; blinded after Suleiman II's installation in January 1750; restored by Ahmad Shah Durrani on 9 May 1755; tortured by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1796.

correction.text: the shape plus Armenia, eastern Georgia (Kartli-Kakheti), Azerbaijan and Derbent: 'by the summer of 1735, Armenia and Georgia were under his rule'; 'the latter agreed to withdraw all of their troops from Iranian territory'

keyframe_review.note: The shape (1.59 M km2, Iran, the Herat side of Afghanistan and part of Azerbaijan) holds for 1736-1737, the Afsharid years; in 1734-1735 it is Safavid land under Nader's regency ('In 1732 he forced Tahmasp to abdicate in favour of the Shah's infant son, Abbas III'). The page has 'by the summer of 1735, Armenia and Georgia were under his rule', the Treaty of Ganja (March 1735) with Russia leaving Iranian territory (Derbent, Baku and Tarki) and a 1736 Treaty of Constantinople confirming Iranian suzerainty over the Caucasus, none of which the shape holds (Yerevan, Tbilisi, Baku and Derbent are outside). The infobox gives no area, so no comparison; the Nader Shah page has no 1736 treaty.

correction.text: the shape plus all of Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul and Peshawar, taken in 1738

keyframe_review.note: 2.75 M km2. 'In 1738, Nader Shah conquered Kandahar'; Ghazni on 11 June, Kabul on 19 June (the citadel 'capitulated after a week-long siege') and Peshawar occupied three days after 6 November 1738. The shape holds only 3 of 7 Kandahar cells and not Peshawar; Georgia and Armenia are in, as the page has them. Bahrain (2 of 3 cells) is 'recaptured from the Arabs' on an undated page sentence.

intersect.text: east of the Indus between Attock and the Sindh border

union.text: Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus

correction.text: the shape without Delhi, Lahore and the Indian cells east of the Indus: 'Nader ceded back to Muhammad Shah all territories to the east of the Indus'; fx-10: also without Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus

keyframe_review.note: 3.43 M km2 with Delhi and Lahore (4 of 4 cells) and 473 Indian cells. The page has Nader leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739 after he 'ceded back to Muhammad Shah all territories to the east of the Indus'; the infobox says he annexed 'all lands west of the Indus river'. Remove everything east of the Indus. Oman and Muscat are in the shape from 1741 but the pages date the conquest 'in 1743'; Khiva and Bukhara are outside, as vassals (1740). Balochistan and the Sindh part of Pakistan (2,253 of 3,277 cells) are on no dated page. Fix fx-10 (1 Nov 2026): the minus left Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus in the shape (340 cells in 1741, 4 in 1744, all also in mughal-empire's keyframes). Nader Shah's invasion page (opened 2026-11-01): before leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739 he 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'. mughal-empire's 1741 keyframe now restores that land and drops the land west of the Indus, so the two shapes meet at the river.

intersect.text: east of the Indus between Attock and the Sindh border

union.text: Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus

correction.text: the shape without the cells east of the Indus; fx-10: also without Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus

keyframe_review.note: 3.46 M km2. The same east-of-Indus cells (631 Indian cells, Delhi 2 of 4) remain although the page has them ceded back in 1739. Eastern Georgia is out of the shape, which matches 1744 when 'Georgian rulers Erekle II and Teimuraz II were made kings by Nader' (they are drawn as vassals). Iraq (163 cells) is the Kirkuk-Erbil front of the war of 1743-1746, which ended 'status quo ante bellum', so it is not a gain. Fix fx-10 (1 Nov 2026): the minus left Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus in the shape (340 cells in 1741, 4 in 1744, all also in mughal-empire's keyframes). Nader Shah's invasion page (opened 2026-11-01): before leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739 he 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'. mughal-empire's 1741 keyframe now restores that land and drops the land west of the Indus, so the two shapes meet at the river.

correction.text: Khorasan (Mashhad) and Herat until the Durrani siege of 1750-51

keyframe_review.note: 1.75 M km2 with Tabriz, Tehran, Mazandaran, Khuzestan and the Indus lands. After Nader's death (20 June 1747) the Afsharid state is Shahrokh's: 'He ruled western Khorasan, roughly the present-day Khorasan Province, from 1748 to 1796', proclaimed at Mashhad on 1 October 1748. Herat, which Nader had given the child Shahrokh, falls to Ahmad Shah Durrani 'shortly after his 1750 restoration'. The Durrani Empire is founded in 1747 and the Zands and others hold the rest. The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Khorasan around Mashhad, Shahrokh's land under Durrani pressure and then Durrani overlordship

keyframe_review.note: 0.93 M km2 with Tabriz and Tehran. Shahrokh's land in these years is Khorasan: 'Ahmad Shah's siege of Mashhad was abandoned in early 1751'; he was 'officially restored as king' on 9 May 1755 after the Durrani march on Khorasan of 1 May 1754 (the Afsharid page: 'subjected to the Durranis in the second Durrani campaign, 1754-55'). The Durrani Empire holds Herat.

New keyframe: Cliopatria's Afsharid row stops in 1756 but the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1796' and Shahrokh 'ruled western Khorasan ... from 1748 to 1796'. The rump state is drawn as Khorasan until Agha Mohammad Khan 'seized Mashhad and tortured Shahrokh' in 1796; under the Durrani overlordship of 1755 (the Afsharid page) the durrani-empire dossier should hold the matching vassal event. After Ahmad Shah's death in 1772 'Kurdish chieftains ruled over several fortresses, such as Bojnord and Quchan' (Shahrokh page), a loss of the north-east that the page does not date.

region.text: Armenia, eastern Georgia and the Caucasus

ledger.note: 1736: the Ottomans confirm Iranian rule in the Caucasus. 'The Treaty of Constantinople [1736] forced the Ottomans to confirm Iranian suzerainty over the Caucasus.' The Nader Shah page has no 1736 treaty (its only Constantinople treaty is of 1724), so the year rests on the Afsharid page.

region.text: the Safavid lands under Nader's regency: Iran, Herat and the Caucasus

ledger.note: 22 January 1736: Nader's assembly on the Mughan plain makes him shah. Infobox 'Established: 22 January 1736'; the body has the qoroltai in January 1736 and 'Nader was crowned Shah of Iran on March 8, 1736'. Ahead of this, in 1732 he made Abbas III shah and ruled as regent; by summer 1735 'Armenia and Georgia were under his rule' and the Treaty of Ganja (March 1735) had Russia 'withdraw all of their troops from Iranian territory' (Derbent, Baku, Tarki).
Early 1737: Nader's army camps at Kandahar. 'Early 1737: Nader Shah's camp near Kandahar, where he founded Naderabad.' The siege lasts into 1738.
1738: Kandahar falls. 'In 1738, Nader Shah conquered Kandahar, the last outpost of the Hotak dynasty.'
1738: the Hotaki are finished at Kandahar.

1738 (Cliopatria's year, page undated): Bahrain. 'He recaptured the island of Bahrain from the Arabs' stands without a year among the Persian Gulf operations of 1737-1744 (the Nader Shah page: Iran 'lost Bahrain to the House of Khalifa in 1783').

region.text: Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar and the Punjab, the Mughal marches

ledger.note: June 1738: the campaign against the Mughals opens. He reached Ghazni on 11 June (another passage says 31 May); 'the citadel of Kabul capitulated after a week-long siege' on 19 June 1738.
June 1738: Ghazni and Kabul. 'Nader left Naderabad for Kabul' on 21 May; Ghazni reached 11 June; Kabul capitulated 19 June; Jalalabad was sacked on 7 September 1738.
November 1738: Peshawar. On 6 November the march toward India resumed and 'the Mughal army was destroyed at the Khyber Pass, and Peshawar was occupied three days later'.
20 March 1739: Nader enters Delhi; the massacre begins on 22 March (20,000-30,000 dead). Karnal was fought on 24 February 1739 on this page (the Afsharid page says 13 February).
16 May 1739: Nader leaves Delhi (the Afsharid page: 'at the beginning of May 1739').

region.text: Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar and the Punjab, the Mughal marches

ledger.note: May 1739: the war ends with the Indus as the boundary. 'Before leaving Delhi, he ceded back the territories east of the Indus to Muhammad Shah'; the infobox says he annexed 'all lands west of the Indus river'; an indemnity of 20 million rupees was levied on Delhi.

region.text: Sindh, among the lands west of the Indus annexed in May 1739

ledger.note: May 1739: Sindh, among the lands west of the Indus. The invasion page has Nader 'annexes all lands west of the Indus river' (infobox) and, leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739, he 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus'; the Afsharid page lists Sindh among the captures of the campaign ('This led to the capture of Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar, Sindh and Lahore') without a year. Reviewer me-10-c moved this event from 1741 (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1) to May 1739 to match the page and the mughal-empire loss of May 1739. The page draws no line inside Sindh; the region keeps the province as the 1741 shape does.
1740: Bukhara submits. 'After Bukhara was forced to submit, Nader married the khan's daughter.' The page gives no Oxus boundary terms.
1740: Khiva is conquered. 'In 1740 he conquered Khanate of Khiva'; the khanate survives, so it is drawn as a vassal.
1741: the Dagestan campaign. 'Nader managed to take most of Dagestan during his campaign' but was later forced to withdraw; the infobox dates the campaign 1741-1745.

region.text: Oman and its main capital Muscat

ledger.note: 1743: Oman. 'In 1743, he conquered Oman and its main capital Muscat.' The Ahmad bin Said page has Persian forces holding Muscat, and Taqi Khan confirming Ahmad as governor of Sohar and Barka after a nine-month siege.

region.text: Kirkuk, Erbil and the Kars front

ledger.note: 1743: war with the Ottomans. Nader declared war in 1743 and 'captured both' Kirkuk and Erbil that year; Mosul was besieged from 14 September 1743 for about 40 days but held out; Kars was besieged unsuccessfully in July 1744 and an Ottoman army was routed there in August 1745.
1744: Nader makes Erekle II king of Kakheti. 'Georgian rulers Erekle II and Teimuraz II were made kings by Nader in 1744.'
1744: Nader makes Teimuraz II king of Kartli (same sentence).
1745: the Dagestan campaign ends in withdrawal (infobox 1741-1745).

region.text: Kirkuk, Erbil and the Kars front

ledger.note: September 1746: the Treaty of Kerden ends the war. 'The sources date it to September 1746, and one gives 4 September 1746'; the infobox has 'status quo ante bellum' and Baghdad stays Ottoman. The Afsharid page says instead that 'the Ottomans agreed to let Nader occupy Najaf'; the war page does not say so.

1747: the Persians are driven out of Oman. Ahmad bin Said 'invited the remaining Persian troops to a banquet at his fort in Barka' and massacred them; other historians say they 'voluntarily withdrew'.
1747-1748 (page silent): Bahrain and the Gulf coast pass out of Afsharid hands with Nader's death; the Nader Shah page has Iran losing Bahrain only 'to the House of Khalifa in 1783'.
1747 (bridging): Erekle II's Kakheti is free after Nader's death ('Erekle II later unified eastern Georgia as Kartli-Kakheti'); no date on the page.
1747 (bridging): Teimuraz II's Kartli is free after Nader's death.

region.text: the Afghan lands and Peshawar, my reading of the Durrani core

ledger.note: 1747: Ahmad Shah Abdali founds the Durrani Empire. 'After Nader Shah's assassination at the hands of a faction of his officers in 1747' (Nader died on 20 June 1747 at Quchan) Ahmad Shah 'had declared his independence by founding the Durrani Empire'; the page names no lands.
June 1747 (bridging): Khiva and Bukhara cease to be Afsharid vassals with Nader's death on 20 June 1747; no page dates the end of their submission.
June 1747 (bridging): as for Khiva.

region.text: everything the 1744 shape had outside Khorasan

ledger.note: 1748 (page silent on the land): the state shrinks to Shahrokh's Khorasan. The page lists Zand Iran, Qajar Iran and the Durrani Empire among the successors without dates, and Cliopatria's Afsharid shape of 1748 still holds Tabriz and Tehran, which no page gives to Shahrokh.

1750: Ahmad Shah Durrani invades Khorasan. 'Ahmad Shah Durrani launched an invasion into Khorasan and captured Herat after a siege lasting several months', shortly after Suleiman II's installation in January 1750; his siege of Mashhad was 'abandoned in early 1751'.

region.text: Herat, which Nader had made Shahrokh's as a child

ledger.note: 1750: Herat falls to Ahmad Shah (the page: 'shortly after his 1750 restoration', no exact year).
Early 1751: the first Durrani siege of Mashhad is abandoned.
1 May 1754: Ahmad Shah marches on Khorasan again.

9 May 1755: Shahrokh 'officially restored as king' by Ahmad Shah; the Afsharid page: 'subjected to the Durranis in the second Durrani campaign, 1754-55'. The Shahrokh page does not call him a vassal; the durrani-empire dossier should hold the overlordship.

region.text: Khorasan around Mashhad, the last Afsharid land

ledger.note: 1796: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar takes Mashhad. He 'seized Mashhad and tortured Shahrokh', who died at Damghan of his injuries in 1796 (Shahrokh page). Nader Mirza revolted in 1797 and was executed in April 1803.

wars.name: Siege of Kandahar (1737-1738)
wars.outcome: Kandahar, 'the last outpost of the Hotak dynasty', taken in 1738.
wars.note: Naderabad founded as camp in early 1737.

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India

zones.text: Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar and the Punjab

wars.outcome: Mughal army beaten at Karnal on 24 February 1739; Delhi sacked 22 March; Nader leaves 16 May 1739, annexing 'all lands west of the Indus' and ceding back the east; 20 million rupees indemnity.
wars.note: The Afsharid page dates Karnal 13 February 1739, this page 24 February.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Central Asian campaign
wars.outcome: Bukhara forced to submit and Khiva conquered in 1740; both khanates survive.
wars.note: No Oxus boundary terms on the page.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Dagestan campaign
wars.outcome: 'Managed to take most of Dagestan' but 'later forced to withdraw'.

wars.name: Persian invasion of Oman
wars.outcome: Nader's forces take Oman and Muscat in 1743; Ahmad bin Said holds Sohar and Barka as a tributary governor and expels the Persians in 1747.
wars.note: The Oman page has the Persians in Oman 'on two occasions between 1737 and 1744'.

wars.name: Ottoman-Persian War (1743-1746)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Kerden, September 1746: status quo ante bellum; Nader's demand for Ja'fari recognition dropped.
wars.note: The Afsharid page has the Ottomans agreeing to let Nader occupy Najaf; the war page does not.

wars.name: Durrani invasions of Khorasan
wars.outcome: Herat lost to Ahmad Shah in 1750; Mashhad besieged until early 1751; Shahrokh restored as king on 9 May 1755 after the second Durrani campaign.
wars.note: The page does not describe Shahrokh as a vassal.

certainty.note: The Caucasus, Indus and Oxus frontiers are military lines; the nearest to treaty lines are the Indus boundary of May 1739 and the Ottoman frontier restored by the Treaty of Kerden (September 1746).
Shahrokh's Khorasan has no surveyed edge and shrinks and recovers under Durrani pressure.

notes: Page budget (5 pages) spent; the Ahmad bin Said page was opened for the sultanate-of-oman dossier. No page gives an area (the infobox has only 9,000,000 population for 1736-1747, 6,000,000 after). Disagreements: Established 22 January 1736 (infobox) vs coronation 8 March 1736 (body and Nader Shah page); Karnal 13 February 1739 (Afsharid page) vs 24 February 1739 (Invasion of India page); Nader left Delhi 'beginning of May' (Afsharid) vs 16 May (Invasion of India); Ghazni 11 June or 31 May 1738; the Afsharid page has a 1736 Treaty of Constantinople, the Nader Shah page does not and its only Constantinople treaty is of 1724; Najaf occupied under Kerden (Afsharid) vs status quo ante bellum (war page). Cliopatria rows: the 1734 shape runs two years before the dynasty (Nader is regent of the Safavids, so those years belong to safavid-dynasty); 1741 and 1744 shapes keep Delhi and the Indian cells; 1748-1756 shapes are wrong for Shahrokh's Khorasan (they hold Tabriz, Tehran, Mazandaran); the row stops in 1756 though the infobox ends 1796 (a new keyframe 1757-1796 carries Khorasan). Not on any page opened: Balochistan and the Sindh/Pakistan cells of 1741-1747 (Kalat is a successor in the infobox), the Persian Gulf coast and islands (Bandar Abbas region), the Khanate of Kalat, the dates of Bahrain's capture and loss, Nader Mirza's rule of Mashhad 1797-1803 (a rebel claim after the end). The durrani-empire dossier should record Shahrokh as its vassal from May 1755; the Georgian kings (kingdom-of-georgia, kingdom-of-kakheti) as Afsharid vassals 1744-1747. Counterparts needing dossiers: Dagestani tribes and khanates (Avar Khanate etc.); the Arab rulers of Bahrain.
